To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the fractal picture of QCD jet evolution is confirmed by the analysis of QCD corrections to jet cross-sections, that the jet calculus can be constructed beyond the leading order in a systematic manner, and that the construction of the generalized Altarelli Parisi parton decay function is a nontrivial task.

the QCD jet picture is fractal, the jet calculus vertices can be constructed in a systematic way, and that the next-to-leading order corrections to the jet calculus vertices and parton decay functions are calculable.

the fractal picture of QCD in LLA is confirmed, that the LLA description of QCD in terms of jet calculus is extended to next-to-leading logarithms, and that the next-to-leading order corrections are small, but not negligible.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the description of QCD jet events in the framework of perturbative QCF.
the following three topics: 1) the intuitive (fractality) and quantitative picture of QCD jet structure; 2) the jet calculus and its applications; 3) QCD jet structure beyond the leading order.

the following questions: What is the intuitive (fractile) picture of QCD jet? What are the quantitative features of QCD jets? What are the QCD corrections beyond leading order to the intuitive picture? What are the next-to-leading order corrections to the jet calculus?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
QCD is a very rich subject, and we are still far from a final understanding of its basic features.

the intuitive fractal picture of QCD is well founded and that its quantitative realization is possible in principle, but that the present state of the art is still far from being able to provide a complete quantitative description.
the QCD jet picture, in the leading log as well as beyond it, is a consistent one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the jet picture of QCD is a well-established concept in perturbative Q.C.D. at the leading log approximation, and that the jet picture is also valid at the next-to-leading log approximation.
, in LLA, QCD jets are characterized by a fractal structure with a universal branching function.
the jet calculus is an effective tool for the description of the QCD cascade at the parton level, and is applicable to the description of the hadronization process as well.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the leading order, the fractal structure of QCD jets is well captured by the LLA jet calculus and its generalizations, but that the fractal structure is broken in the next-to-leading order.
the picture of QDC jets as a fractal object, with a fractal dimension, is a robust concept that can be extended beyond the leading order of perturbation theory.
the jet calculus is a useful tool for describing QCD jets beyond the leading order and for testing the universality of QCD jets.
